title: Time, days & months
goal: Tell the time, name the days of the week and parts of the day, and talk about today, yesterday and tomorrow.
intro:
Pashtun daily life is shaped by the five daily prayers, the Friday congregational prayer and the seasons. Afghanistan uses the **solar Hijri calendar**, whose months have beautiful Pashto names taken from the zodiac (وری 'the Ram', غويی 'the Bull' …); Pakistan uses the Western calendar for official purposes; and everyone uses the **lunar Islamic calendar** for Ramadan and Eid.

In this unit you'll learn to tell the time, the days of the week, and the most useful time expressions.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.body:
Ask **څو بجې دي؟** (tso báje di?, 'how many o'clocks are they?'). Answer with the number + **بجې** + **دي**: پنځه بجې دي 'it's five o'clock'. One o'clock is singular: **يوه بجه ده**.

Half past is **نيمې** (níme), which agrees with the plural بجې: څلور نيمې بجې 'half past four' — but half past one is singular, **يوه نيمه بجه**. A quarter is **پاو** (pāw): درې بجې او پاو 'quarter past three' (also سوا درې بجې), پاو کم څلور بجې 'quarter to four'. For other times, add minutes with **او** 'and': درې بجې او پنځلس دقيقې 'three fifteen'; or count down: څلورو بجو ته لس دقيقې پاتې دي '(it's) ten minutes to four' (lit. to four o'clock ten minutes remain).

'At' a time uses **په** + the oblique plural in **-o**: په دوو بجو 'at two', په پنځو بجو 'at five', په لسو بجو 'at ten'. For one o'clock: په يوه بجه (more formally په يوې بجې).

examples.native: لس بجې او شل دقيقې دي.
examples.roman: las báje aw shəl daqiqé di.

examples.native: زه په پنځو بجو کور ته ځم.
examples.roman: zə pə pindzó bajó kor ta dzəm.
examples.en: I go home at five o'clock.

grammar.title: Days, months and time expressions
grammar.body:
Time words usually come at the **start** of the sentence or right after the subject, and need no preposition: **نن** سهار 'this morning', **پرون** ماښام 'yesterday evening', **سبا** 'tomorrow', **هره ورځ** 'every day', **بله اوونۍ** 'next week', **تېره مياشت** 'last month'. 'At night' is د شپې, 'at noon' د غرمې.

For a day of the week say **د … په ورځ** 'on the day of …': د جمعې په ورځ 'on Friday'.

**Afghan solar months** (from 21 March): وری wray, غويی ġwayáy, غبرګولی ġbargólay, چنګاښ changā́ṣ, زمری zmaráy, وږی waẓáy, تله tə́la, لړم laṛám, ليندۍ lində́y, مرغومی marġúmay, سلواغه salwā́ġa, کب kab.
**Western months** (used in Pakistan): جنوري، فبروري، مارچ، اپرېل، مۍ، جون، جولای، اګست، سپتمبر، اکتوبر، نومبر، ډسمبر.
The Islamic months include روژه rozhá (Ramadan, also 'the fast').

examples.en: It was very cold this morning.

examples.native: د جمعې په ورځ جومات ته ځو.
examples.roman: də jumʿé pə wradz jumā́t ta dzu.
examples.en: On Friday we go to the mosque.
I get up early every day.

examples.native: زما د زوکړې ورځ د وري په لومړۍ ده.
examples.roman: zmā də zokṛé wradz də wrí pə lumṛə́y da.
examples.en: My birthday is on the first of Wray (21 March).
Next week I'm going to Kabul.

dialogue.title: Catching the bus
dialogue.setting: Nazo and her brother Zalmay are getting ready to travel from Jalalabad to Kabul.

lines.speaker: Nazo
lines.en: What time does the bus leave?

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: په اتو بجو. وخت نشته، ژر شه!
lines.roman: pə ató bajó. waxt nə́shta, zhər sha!
lines.en: At eight. There's no time — hurry up!

lines.speaker: Nazo
lines.native: تل همداسې وايې! کابل ته څو ساعته لار ده؟
lines.roman: tal hamdā́se wā́ye! kābúl ta tso sāʿáta lār da?
lines.en: You always say that! How many hours is it to Kabul?

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: درې يا څلور ساعته. د غرمې هلته يو.
lines.roman: dre yā tsalór sāʿáta. də ġárme hálta yu.
lines.en: Three or four hours. We'll be there by noon.

lines.speaker: Nazo
lines.en: And when are we coming back?

lines.speaker: Zalmay
lines.native: د پنجشنبې په ورځ، انشاالله. جمعه په کور کې يو.
lines.roman: də panjshanbé pə wradz, inshāllā́h. jumʿá pə kor ke yu.
lines.en: On Thursday, God willing. We'll be home for Friday.

lines.speaker: Nazo
lines.native: سمه ده. زه تياره يم، ځه چې ځو!
lines.roman: sáma da. zə tayā́ra yəm, dza che dzu!

culture: The day is often described by the prayer times rather than the clock: د سهار لمونځ (dawn), ماسپښين (afternoon), ماښام (sunset), ماخستن (night prayer) — 'I'll come after ماسپښين' is a normal appointment. Punctuality is relaxed in social life, but Friday prayers at midday are a fixed point, and many shops close for them. Afghan New Year (نوی کال, نوروز) falls on 1 Wray (21 March), celebrated with picnics and the first flowers of spring; in Pakistan the Western new year matters more. During **روژه** (Ramadan) daily life shifts: people eat before dawn (پېشمني peshmanə́y) and break the fast at sunset (روژه ماتي).

tip.title: Telling the time
tip.body:
- Number + **بجې** + **دي**: پنځه بجې دي 'it's five'. One o'clock is singular: **يوه بجه ده**.
- Half past: **نيمې** بجې (but يوه **نيمه** بجه). Quarter: **پاو** — درې بجې او پاو 'quarter past three', پاو کم څلور بجې 'quarter to four'.
- Minutes are added with **او**: نهه بجې او لس دقيقې.
tip.pattern: څو بجې دي؟ — پنځه بجې دي

sentences.native: نهه بجې او لس دقيقې دي.
sentences.roman: nə́hə báje aw las daqiqé di.

sentences.native: اوس اته بجې او پنځلس دقيقې دي.
sentences.roman: os atə́ báje aw pindzə́las daqiqé di.

tip.title: 'At' a time: په … بجو
tip.body:
- 'At five' is **په** پنځ**و** **بجو**: the number and بجې both take **-o**.
- په لسو بجو 'at ten', په اتو بجو 'at eight'; one o'clock is **په يوه بجه**.
- **د سهار** in the morning · **د غرمې** at noon · **د ماښام** in the evening · **د شپې** at night.

sentences.native: زه په شپږو بجو کور ته ځم.
sentences.roman: zə pə shpaẓó bajó kor ta dzəm.

sentences.native: د سهار په اتو بجو ناشته کوو.
sentences.roman: də sahā́r pə ató bajó nāshtá kawú.
sentences.en: We have breakfast at eight in the morning.

sentences.native: د ماښام ډوډۍ په نهو بجو ده.
sentences.roman: də māṣā́m ḍoḍə́y pə nəhó bajó da.

sentences.native: د غرمې ډوډۍ په يوه بجه ده.
sentences.roman: də ġárme ḍoḍə́y pə yáwa bája da.

tip.title: Time words come first
tip.body:
- **نن** today, **پرون** yesterday, **سبا** tomorrow need no preposition and usually start the sentence: سبا کابل ته ځم.
- **هره ورځ** every day (ورځ is feminine, so هر → هره).
- The present often covers the near future: سبا راځم 'I'll come tomorrow'.
tip.pattern: نن / پرون / سبا + rest of the sentence

sentences.native: ته نن په کور کې يې؟
sentences.roman: tə nən pə kor ke ye?

sentences.native: سبا سهار په اتو بجو راځم.
sentences.roman: sabā́ sahā́r pə ató bajó rā́dzəm.
sentences.en: I'll come tomorrow morning at eight.

sentences.native: زه هره ورځ پښتو زده کوم.
sentences.roman: zə hára wradz paṣtó zdə kawə́m.

sentences.native: سهار مو په خير، حاجي صاحب!
sentences.roman: sahā́r mo pə xayr, hājí sāhíb!

sentences.native: شپه دې په خير، احمد جان.
sentences.roman: shpa de pə xayr, ahmád jān.

tip.title: 'On Monday': د … په ورځ
tip.body:
- Say 'on the day of …': **د** دوشنب**ې** **په ورځ** 'on Monday'.
- All the day names are feminine in -a, so after د they end in **-e**: جمعه → د جمع**ې**.
- The Afghan week starts on شنبه (Saturday); جمعه (Friday) is the day off.

sentences.native: د دوشنبې په ورځ کابل ته ځم.
sentences.roman: də doshanbé pə wradz kābúl ta dzəm.
sentences.en: I'm going to Kabul on Monday.

sentences.native: د سه‌شنبې په ورځ په کور کې نه يم.
sentences.roman: də seshanbé pə wradz pə kor ke na yəm.
sentences.en: I'm not at home on Tuesday.

sentences.native: د چهارشنبې په ورځ ته چېرته يې؟
sentences.roman: də chārshanbé pə wradz tə chérta ye?

sentences.native: د پنجشنبې په ورځ مېلمانه راځي.
sentences.roman: də panjshanbé pə wradz melmānə́ rā́dzi.

sentences.native: د جمعې په ورځ ټوله کورنۍ په کور کې وي.
sentences.roman: də jumʿé pə wradz ṭóla kornə́y pə kor ke wi.
sentences.en: On Fridays the whole family is at home.
No, I don't have time now.

tip.title: Before and after
tip.body:
- **له** … **مخکې** 'before', **له** … **وروسته** 'after': له ډوډۍ وروسته.
- With a length of time, put it first: دوه ساعته **وروسته** 'two hours later, in two hours'.
- **بله** مياشت 'next month', **بله** اوونۍ 'next week' (both feminine).

sentences.en: We drink tea after the meal.
Next month we're going to Kabul.

sentences.native: زه يوه مياشت په کابل کې يم.
sentences.roman: zə yáwa miyā́sht pə kābúl ke yəm.
sentences.en: I'm in Kabul for a month.

sentences.native: ساعت مې په کور کې دی.
sentences.roman: sāʿát me pə kor ke day.

sentences.native: له اتو بجو مخکې کور ته راشه.
sentences.roman: la ató bajó mə́xke kor ta rā́sha.
